comments.content: Code looks good. Please post [QA](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot#how-to-qa-any-additions-to-the-bot)
You have a lot of bugs, next time test your solution and post QA

[pull request reviews](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-reviews-for-a-pull-request) api will only return the reviews which state can be `COMMENT`, `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, or `APPROVED`. I think you need to combine this with [review requests](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/review-requests?apiVersion=2022-11-28#about-review-requests) to see who was requested but didn't leave a review yet, but still that can't be accurate because if the reviewer leaves a review and creator fixes things and requests a review again so you shouldn't count previous reviews.

like I typed - you would use [review requests](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/review-requests?apiVersion=2022-11-28#about-review-requests) to see who was requested and use [pull request reviews](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-reviews-for-a-pull-request) to see who left the review and who didn't.
however this is not accurate as I described above, so you should try to find another way
if that's true, that would be great. can you verify it?
you can use `context.octokit.pulls.listRequestedReviewers`
put it back in the helper function, just wrap it in try/catch because it will throw error so you don't need to check status. you can see other examples in helpers
